title: Capacity Burst Simulator — playbook & wireframe notes
content:
Context and goal:
This doc captures a lightweight playbook + low-fidelity wireframe notes for a Capacity Burst Simulator feature in the Dedicated Capacity console. The intent: let capacity planners, SREs, and platform engineers run fast what-if scenarios against GPU pools, reservation schedules, and autoscale policies so they can understand latency/cost tradeoffs before committing reserved capacity or changing autoscale bounds. Target audience: platform engineers, capacity ops, solutions engineering, and product PMs.

Design constraints and assumptions:
- Model capacity expressed in GPU slots (v100/p4d/nvidia-a100 equivalents) and logical "pool units".
- Simulator must accept realistic traffic distributions (RPS, token-per-request distributions, percent chat vs embed) or replay a short trace (CSV).
- Keep UI light; primary flows are scenario authoring and timeline visualization. Exportable results for SRE runbooks and sales collaterals.
- Should integrate with existing reservation API and autoscale policy model; simulator does not change live config unless user explicitly pushes a plan.

Primary user journeys (high level):
1) Quick pulse: open simulator, pick a pool and a date range (next 24/48 hours), run default "peak+baseline" scenario to validate current config handles expected burst.
2) Reservation planner: create scenario that adds a temporary reservation (X GPUs, start/end), simulate cost/latency impact and get an estimate for overage vs reserved commit.
3) Autoscale tuning: edit autoscale policy (min/max, scale window, priority tiers), run scenario with a synthetic burst shape to validate tail latency and token cost.
4) What-if chaining: combine cache-hit improvements, batch-size changes, and quantization profile to see compound effects.

Wireframe pages & components (low-fi notes):
A. Simulator Home (left nav -> "Burst Simulator")
- Top bar: pool selector (searchable), zone/region dropdown, active model family filter.
- Quick actions row: "Run default pulse", "Create new scenario", "Upload trace".
- Recent scenarios list: small card per scenario with name, last run, key outputs (peak GPU needed, 95p latency, estimated delta cost). Buttons: Run / Clone / Export / Push-to-Plan (disabled for non-admin).
- Small note: show linked reservations currently active for the selected pool (inline pill list).

B. Scenario Builder (canvas split 2-up: left authoring, right results timeline)
Left column fields (author):
- Scenario name (required)
- Input mode toggle: "Synthetic" | "Trace".
- For Synthetic:
  - Traffic shape selector: single-peak, multi-peak, plateau, ramp, stochastic (dropdown).
  - Peak parameters: peak RPS, duration, start offset.
  - Token distribution: mean tokens/request, variance, percent streaming vs non-streaming.
  - Model mix: % gpt-embedding / % gpt-chat / % small-classifier.
- For Trace: upload CSV (timestamp, rps/tokens/model-tag) or paste sample.
- Infrastructure knobs (affect runtime): batch target, max batch latency, KV cache hit%, model quant profile (fp16 / int8 / q4_0), prefix cache enabled toggle.
- Resource actions: add reservation (num gpus, start/end), set autoscale override for scenario (min,max,burst_buffer_pct).
- Run controls: run now / dry-run / compare to baseline checkbox.

Right column (results):
- Timeline chart (stacked): concurrent GPU usage over time; annotation strips for reservations; horizontal lines for pool cap and autoscale max. Hover shows per-minute token cost and 95p latency estimate.
- KPI strip above timeline: peak GPUs needed, 95p inferred latency, total token cost, reserve utilization%. Small colored badges for SLA breach events if any (e.g., "95p latency > 300ms for 4m -> show alert").
- Breakdown tabs: Cost (token + GPU-hour estimates), Latency (latency curve), Ops (expected queue depth, expected failed requests or fallback events), Sensitivity (how much batch size or cache hit% changes outcomes).
- Export button: CSV + Markdown run summary.

C. Reservation Timeline editor (modal / overlay)
- Inline Gantt: show existing reservations as bars; allow drag to extend/shrink.
- Add-on: "temporary reservation" quick-create with templated durations (2h, 8h, 24h) and auto-calc of committed vs on-demand cost.
- Conflict tooltip: if new reservation collides with scheduled bursts marked high-priority, show recommended re-ordering or suggest increasing autoscale max.

D. Autoscale policy editor (compact inline)
- Show effective min/max, cooldown, and priority tiers.
- Add simulated warmup penalty toggle (models that have cold-kernel overhead).
- Quick preview: small sparklines showing how policy would have responded to the last 7 days of observed metrics (replay mode).

Visual / interaction notes:
- Timeline must be zoomable (1h -> 1w). Use condensed representation for long ranges with aggregated max per bucket.
- Use colors consistently: pool caps (dark grey), reserved GPUs (blue), autoscaled (green), forecasted demand (red/orange).
- Keep raw numbers accessible on hover; default view should emphasize clear decisions e.g., "Need +8 GPUs for 3h" card pinned above timeline.

Backlog grooming items (prioritized):
1) Scenario builder MVP (synth traffic + simple autoscale knobs) — 3 sprint points. Acceptance: run synthetic burst, timeline renders, export CSV.
2) Reservation quick-create & cost calc — 2 points. Acceptance: user can add temporary reservation and see cost delta vs on-demand.
3) Autoscale replay visualization (7d) — 2 points.
4) Trace upload & parse (CSV schema + small replay) — 3 points.
5) Sensitivity analysis tab (batch/cache/quant) — 3 points.
6) Push-to-plan workflow (create Jira + apply to staging reservation API) — 5 points (security gated).
7) Multi-pool scenario (combine pools for sharding strategies) — 3 points.
8) Role gating & approvals (enterprise) — 2 points.

Open questions / risks:
- Accuracy of latency model: we currently have a baseline perf table per model/sequence-length; need to validate combined effects of batching + cache hit% with bench data. (Action: Dario to run bench matrix INF-3129).
- How to represent uncertainty: show ranges (p10/p90) or a single estimate? Initial plan: show median + a light shaded band to represent variance.
- UX density: how many knobs are too many for the average user? Consider collapsible `advanced` sections.
- Permissions: Push-to-plan should be restricted. Decide which roles can create committed reservations.

Acceptance criteria (for MVP run):
- User can create a synthetic scenario, run it, and see a timeline with peak GPU usage and at least one cost estimate.
- The scenario overlays existing reservations and flags any SLA breaches in a clear visual.
- Results are exportable and clonable.

Next steps / owner action items:
- Maya: consolidate this doc with figma components and handoff to eng (by 2025-01-17).
- Dario: run latency vs batch/quant bench and share lookup tables (due 2025-01-24).
- Priya: draft UI copy for scenario presets and run result summaries (due 2025-01-20).
- Tom: prototype timeline canvas performance for large traces (due 2025-01-31).

Notes to reviewers (quick):
- Focus feedback on the scenario builder field set (are the knobs the right ones?) and the reseller-facing export summary (is the cost delta explainable?).
- We want a compact path to get "good enough" answers for sales/demo use cases while leaving room to increase fidelity for enterprise customers.

Rough ASCII wireframe (Scenario page, 2-column):
[ Pool selector | Run default ]
+---------------------------------------------------------------+
| Scenario builder         | Timeline results                   |
| - Name                  | [stacked GPU usage chart]          |
| - Traffic: Peak=1200RPS | KPIs: peak=24 GPUs | cost=$550    |
| - Model mix: chat 60%    | Tabs: Cost | Latency | Ops | Sens |
| - infra knobs           | Export | Clone | Push |
+---------------------------------------------------------------+

End of doc.
